source: sars-guide:PAYE-GEN-01-G21 Rev 1 p. 28 (deemed standard employment: required to work less than 22 hours a week and furnishes a written declaration of no other employer; taxed as standard employment)
notes: Required to work 20 hours a week (4 days of 5 hours, R390 a day, 17 days = R6 630 a month = R79 560 a year) and has furnished the written declaration that he/she will not render services to any other employer: deemed standard employment (G21 p. 28), so the tables apply and the amount is under the R99 000 threshold: nil. The calculator already gives nil; this case guards TS-b against taxing deemed-standard staff at a flat 25% (R1 657.50). G21 p. 28 reading used by all the ts-* cases: the deemed-standard bullet has two limbs, (1) under 22 hours a week with a written declaration of no other employer, and (2) at least 5 hours a day and paid under R394 a day, read as an alternative route to deemed standard; the summary-table rows for non-standard employment follow from that (row 5, under 5 hours a day and under R394, is the residual non-standard case taxed at 25%, not a misprint). TS-b must wire taxStatus and the hours into runCase (oracle.ts hard-codes employmentType permanent and passes no taxStatus or unmodelled input today, so this case cannot see them); once wired, this guard must go red if the status is ignored.
